clue.text: Snatch sailor's pipe

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard crossword sailor
a duct is a pipe or channel for fluid or air

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a seaman's tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, the kidnapping sense of snatch.

clue.text: Friendly fellow in a story

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a fable is a short moral story
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A pleasant character appears in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside A FABLE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable describes a good-natured, easy-to-talk-to person, a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Indian capital emerged from citadel Hindus built

indicators.note: what emerged from a phrase was already sitting inside its run of letters

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of one word and the start of the next
surface padding: completes the picture of who built the citadel

explanation.surface: India's capital city grew up around a fortress built by Hindus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' completes the surface picture and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, containing New Delhi, is the seat of India's national government.

clue.text: Minister's chapter left Germany in disarray

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for chapter

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled out of their proper order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A government minister's department has left Germany in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political, but it is the church sense: a minister of religion. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is an ordained member of the Christian clergy, which is what a church minister is.

clue.text: Pop out in Burlesque star's helicopter

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go in, inside the other word

parts.note: Cher starred in the 2010 musical film Burlesque
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A pop star from the film Burlesque steps out of her helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burlesque' looks like an anagram signal but is the film that identifies the star, Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is the everyday informal name for a helicopter, from the sound of its rotors.

clue.text: Will supplement from fish get old chemical company money?

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British chemicals giant
L stands for pound, the British unit of money

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about funding a will's addendum from fish sales and an old chemical firm.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British firm, broken up in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a legal addition that amends or supplements an existing will.

clue.text: Times returned last letter

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so read it from the end

parts.note: two times: AGE, a long period, then MO, a moment

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper sent back the final letter someone wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but two words for spans of time placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the phrase alpha and omega.

clue.text: Prison may result in penny-pinching!

indicators.note: the given letters produce a new arrangement as their outcome

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Jail could lead to a life of scrimping.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme reluctance to spend money, which is what penny-pinching means.

clue.text: Sailor's knocked head over heels by girl — yes, indeed!

indicators.note: turning head over heels flips it upside down, which in a down clue reads it backwards

parts.note: TAR is an old word for a sailor, here turned over
her is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A sailor has been bowled over by a girl, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather!' is an old-fashioned British exclamation of emphatic agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: As a British exclamation, Rather! means certainly or very much so, an enthusiastic yes.

clue.text: Toothache's half gone after taking first nip of brandy

indicators.note: the remaining part follows on after picking up another letter
with half gone, only half of the word's letters stay

parts.note: split into tooth, a COG on a gear wheel, and ache, taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A toothache is half gone after a first sip of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toothache' must be split into two words: a tooth is a COG, and ache loses its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a variety of brandy distilled in the Cognac region of western France.

clue.text: Lie has fooled doctor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, altering its arrangement

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's untruth has tricked the physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the person fooled, but it is a verb telling you to tamper with the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untrue statement, a synonym for a lie.

clue.text: Feel sorry for decapitated bird

indicators.note: losing the head means the word's first letter is dropped

parts.note: to regret something is to feel sorry about it

explanation.surface: Pity the poor bird that has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Provide black belt

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a ring is a band or belt encircling something

explanation.surface: A martial-arts instructor hands out a black belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something, as in bring food to the party, is to supply or provide it.

clue.text: Spoon and dish expressly for fruit?

indicators.note: to express something is to put it into speech, so we go by sound

parts.note: to spoon is to kiss and cuddle, or neck; a tureen is a serving dish

explanation.surface: Is a spoon and bowl made specially for eating fruit?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoon' is not cutlery but the old verb for canoodling, which also gives NECK. The question mark flags the loose sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: I left medicine for distribution in a particular area

indicators.note: distributing things spreads them about into a new order
something that has left has gone away, so it is removed

parts.note: the letter that departs
taken as written, before one of its two I's goes

explanation.surface: A doctor has set aside drugs to be handed out in a certain region.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is native to, or regularly found in, a particular place or population.

clue.text: Daughter starts off whingeing as it's raining a bit

indicators.note: with its start taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
to grizzle is to whine or complain fretfully, as a child does

explanation.surface: A daughter begins moaning because it's spitting with rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Grizzling is British for a child's fretful whining; it loses its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Drizzling means light rain falling in fine drops, so raining only a little.

clue.text: Half of lime for Queen's alternative to alcoholic drink

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: the first half of this word
Qu. is an abbreviation for queen
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone offers the Queen a lime cordial instead of strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor means strong alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: Puts rider in and completes course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: adds a condition or reservation to a statement
second meaning: gains a professional certificate by finishing training

explanation.surface: A jockey is fielded and finishes the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing picture is a decoy: a rider is a clause added to a statement or document.
explanation.definitionFit: To qualify a remark is to limit it with a proviso; to qualify as a nurse is to pass the required training.

clue.text: Join forces with UN soldiers retreating to base camp

indicators.note: troops retreating go backwards, so these words are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: the base of a word written across is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: Enlist alongside United Nations troops pulling back to base camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base camp' looks like a single place; it is the base, or last letter, of camp.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up is to enlist, which is to join the armed forces.

clue.text: Shakespearean dismisses love with flourish!

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest
love is nil in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean actor waves away romance with a theatrical gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' looks like a showy gesture but is the verb meaning to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, the verb sense of flourish.

clue.text: Shrink articles on dress style taking a quarter out

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, so the letters are rearranged
taking something out removes it from the word

parts.note: the two indefinite articles, an and a
taken as written, before losing a letter
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A therapist discusses fashion articles, dropping a section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' is slang for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst. 'dress style' reads as a fashion term, but dress is a separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is informal for a psychiatrist; an analyst is a psychoanalyst, the same profession.

clue.text: Donkeys carrying a ton of goods

indicators.note: pack animals carrying a load hold it within them

parts.note: asses are donkeys
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: Pack animals bear a heavy load of merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are possessions of value, and goods are movable property, so both name what someone owns.

clue.text: Play with posh offspring at Hamleys, say

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: read as off-spring: letters that spring off fly loose and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Wealthy children having fun at a famous London toy store.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamleys is a famous toy store on Regent Street, London. 'offspring' looks like children but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamleys is an example of a toyshop; 'say' marks it as one instance of the category.

clue.text: Cross in defeat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to oppose or frustrate someone
second meaning: to foil or prevent from succeeding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but here it is the verb meaning to oppose someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan is to cross it or defeat it, preventing someone from achieving their aim.

clue.text: Unending fog on a little road round bends is dangerous …

indicators.note: with no ending the word loses its final letter

parts.note: haze is a light fog or mist
taken as written
Rd is the short form of road
O is round in shape
U-bends: a hairpin bend is shaped like a U, and two of them are Us

explanation.surface: Endless fog on a narrow road full of curves is risky, so the next clue continues.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazardous means full of risk, a direct synonym of dangerous.

clue.text: Egg's found in strange sort of place for birds to nest

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters are made unfamiliar
something found in another is sitting within it

parts.note: the letters of this word, rearranged
an egg is shaped like an O

explanation.surface: An egg turns up in an odd kind of nesting place.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes after the first letter of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch or place where birds settle to rest or sleep.

clue.text: … suggest travel on motorway coming back

indicators.note: a word coming back travels the other way, so it is read from right to left
placed on, the first-named piece is written after the other one

parts.note: M1, Britain's first motorway, written backwards
to ply is to travel a route regularly, as a ferry does

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: the road is dangerous, which hints at taking the motorway home.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; 1 is read as the letter I. 'on' puts the travel word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to hint at or suggest something without saying it outright.

clue.text: Design super handbag for American girl

indicators.note: to design is to plan a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion instruction to create a great bag for a US girl.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a purse is a small coin wallet; in American English it is a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage purse is the ordinary word for a woman's handbag.

clue.text: Mia organised leave with friend from Madrid

indicators.note: organising things sets them into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of this name, rearranged
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Mia arranged her departure with a Spanish pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, and Madrid stands for Spain.

clue.text: Father's taking a trip, playing bridge

indicators.note: playing with things moves them about into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words, rearranged
an arch is a curved structure spanning a gap, as a bridge does

explanation.surface: Dad is going on holiday and playing cards along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing bridge' looks like the card game, but playing works on the trip words and bridge stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family, a father figure.

clue.text: Cat having hard time gets meaner

indicators.note: the outer word has, or holds, the others inside it

parts.note: the tiger is a big cat
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cat going through a rough patch turns nastier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meaner' looks like nastier but means stingier, more tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for stingy, so tighter means more miserly, which is meaner with money.

clue.text: Snake swallowing up fish becomes dormant

indicators.note: a word going up is written bottom to top, read backwards
what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: the asp is a small venomous snake
the eel is a long fish, here turned around

explanation.surface: A snake, after eating a fish, goes still.
explanation.definitionFit: Asleep and dormant both describe being inactive or at rest, as an animal sleeping off a meal.
